subject: Renewal: cross-region capacity, data escrow & APAC on-ramp
messages:
From: Sinead O'Leary <sinead.oleary@aureliahealth.eu>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T08:14:00Z
Subject: Renewal: cross-region capacity, data escrow & APAC on-ramp

Hi Vanessa,

We're starting our renewal conversations for Aurelia (contract ends 2027-06-30) and wanted to capture two new asks that will drive the shape of the next SOW:

1) APAC on-ramp: we want a staged APAC rollout (Singapore primary, Tokyo standby) with warm standby capacity for peak hours in APAC.
2) Data escrow + residency carveouts: our compliance team is asking about a limited data-escrow arrangement for a subset of audit logs and the ability to keep EU customer data strictly in EU nodes (no cross-border replication for those classes).

Attached is a short PDF with our compliance checklist and a proposed capacity table (proposed_capacity_sku.xlsx).

High level asks from our side: term extension to 24 months, a modest unit price uplift for guaranteed warm-standby APAC capacity, and a path for data-escrow escrow arrangement (legal to confirm). Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a technical and contractual approach for the EU-only residency plus an APAC warm-standby option?

Thanks,
Sinead O'Leary
VP of Infrastructure, Aurelia Health Systems
--
Aurelia Health Systems
phone: +44 20 7946 0700
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sinead O'Leary <sinead.oleary@aureliahealth.eu>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T10:09:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal: cross-region capacity, data escrow & APAC on-ramp

Thanks Sinead — appreciate the clear ask and attachments. Quick response while I pull in product and pricing:

- Technically, we can isolate EU customer data to EU nodes via tenancy + routing policies and prevent automated cross-region replication for marked data classes.
- APAC warm-standby is doable; we'll propose a staged SKU with a guaranteed hourly baseline and a burst rate for peak windows.
- Data escrow for a subset of audit logs is something we can set up as an add-on (encrypted export to an escrow location, retention per your policy) but we need legal/ops alignment on delivery and custody.

I'll loop in Ben (capacity/pricing) and Priyom (legal/ops constraints) and follow up with a draft amendment and a proposed capacity SKU by Tuesday.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal: cross-region capacity, data escrow & APAC on-ramp

Vanessa — quick notes on capacity & pricing assumptions so we can put numbers in the amendment:

Assumptions (from Aurelia attachment + Sinead call):
- Current baseline: 10k requests/hour EU primetime (rolling 95th)
- Projected APAC peak demand: additional 6k requests/hour during 03:00-09:00 UTC
- Warm-standby desired capacity: 30% of peak (~2k rps baseline allocated in APAC, with burst to 6k)

Proposed pricing model:
- Add dedicated APAC standby pool (reserved nodes) with a monthly reserved fee + per-token burst usage at a discounted overage rate.
- Term: 24 months; we can offer a 7% discount off the list for the 24-month commit if they commit to the reserved baseline plus 6 months of committed burst credits.

Operational notes for Priyom:
- Data-escrow: this will require an SOW for export cadence, escrow provider acceptance, and an encrypted key transfer mechanism (customer KMS or HSM).
- EU-only residency enforcement: need a route-block for replication plus routing-level tagging on customer payloads. We'll need Ops playbook updates.

I'll draft the capacity table (attached as proposed_capacity_sku.xlsx) and the price lines and share for sign-off.

Ben
Head of Sales Engineering
From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal: cross-region capacity, data escrow & APAC on-ramp

Quick legal/ops check and constraints:

- We can do EU-only residency for the defined data classes, but the Tech Addendum must explicitly enumerate the data classes and the enforcement points (ingress tagging, tenant-level routing, KV/cache partitioning).
- Data escrow: recommend a scoped offering — only audit logs and non-PII telemetry. Full dataset escrow has heavy compliance overhead and is not recommended unless legal signs off on on-prem transfer requirements.
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS acceptable for escrow keys; we'll need a key escrow handoff procedure in the SOW.
- SLA: Adding APAC standby may change failure/fallback behaviors; propose explicit fallback policy in the amendment: EU primary -> APAC standby on predefined latency/availability triggers; and a manual failover for jurisdictional constraints.

Action items for contract draft:
1) Tech Addendum with data classes and enforcement controls (Ops)
2) Escrow SOW (scope, cadence, provider, key custody)
3) Pricing lines for reserved APAC baseline + burst credits (Ben)
4) Runbook for failover and forensics (Marissa)

I'll coordinate with Legal to get template language by Friday.

- Priyom
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Sinead O'Leary <sinead.oleary@aureliahealth.eu>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@aureliahealth.eu>
Date: 2027-05-06T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal: cross-region capacity, data escrow & APAC on-ramp

Thanks Vanessa — and thanks to your team for the speedy review. Aurelia is comfortable moving forward on the following tentative guardrails:

- 24 month term with the proposed reserved APAC baseline and burst credits (Sinead and Daniel to sign off internally on pricing).
- EU-only residency for "EU Customer Records" (Sinead: we will provide the data class definitions by 2027-05-10).
- Scoped escrow for audit logs only; please include export cadence options (daily/weekly) and a description of the escrow key custody process.

Next steps from our side: internal approval and send a short list of required data classes. From Redwood's side: please share the draft amendment + Tech Addendum + the proposed capacity SKU and pricing (we prefer a single redlined PDF or DocuSign-ready packet).

Once we have the draft we'll route to Procurement and Legal in parallel.

Regards,
Sinead O'Leary
VP of Infrastructure, Aurelia Health Systems

Attachments referenced: Aurelia_Renewal_Request_2027.pdf, proposed_capacity_sku.xlsx
DocuSign ready: please send link when draft is ready.
